mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 3 months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the median market return at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation (>4% YoY CPI).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant in a regression.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both fall for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the joint effect is not statistically significant after controlling for single-variable effects.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate coinciding with a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) over three months signals a deepening labor market downturn, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls for 3 months
regime_hint: labor market stress with weak payroll growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the interaction between UNRATE and PAYEMS does not explain a statistically significant portion of return variance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by the inverse of RSAFS growth) combined with a decline in consumer spending (GDPC1) over six months signals a shift from consumption to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth negative AND GDPC1 flat or falling for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies meet the condition, or the interaction effect is not robust in out-of-sample tests.
